players.note: Sam LaPorta didn't do much last week with a wonderful matchup. Over his last three games, he has had a 73.9% route share with only a 13.3% target share, 1.22 YPRR, two red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 12.2% first-read share. It's been shocking how little he has been utilized. LaPorta looks like he's headed for another down game this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the tenth-fewest yards per target and the ninth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Harold Fannin Jr. is the TE8 in fantasy points per game. He has a 17.7% target share with 1.68 YPRR, four red zone targets, two deep targets, and an 18.1% first-read share. Fannin is a sit this week. Houston has been amazing against tight ends. Over their last five games, they have held the position to the second-fewest yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity. Consider streaming a tight end this week instead of playing Fannin.

Last week, Dalton Kincaid saw his snap rate and route share tumble as the Bills trotted out Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes more, given their need to protect Josh Allen and run the ball. Dalton Kincaid had only a 50.6% snap rate and 47.2% route share. Kincaid's route share has dipped below 60% in three of his last five games. His usage is still fickle this season as it depends upon the matchups and Buffalo's game plan. When he has been on the field, Kincaid has still commanded targets with a 24% TPRR with 2.66 YPRR, six red zone targets, five deep targets, and a 20.3% first-read share. Kincaid's range of outcomes is wide again this week. The Jets have been bleeding out production to tight ends, but over their last five games they also have the fourth-best pressure rate. Kincaid could be heavily utilized this week or nerfed with a 40-50% route share. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Last week, as he played through a foot injury, Hunter Henry had only a 50.8% snap rate, a 47.8% route share, a 7.3% target share, and a 10% first-read share. Hunter Henry managed limited practices all week. He doesn't have an injury designation this week, but that doesn't really mean anything to me. The Pats have talented rookie Eli Raridon who can take some of the lifting this week off Henry's plate as he plays through this foot injury. Henry could see a bump in his routes this week, making him a smash play, but I also won't be shocked if he is a part-time player again in Week 10. Overall, Henry has had a 12.8% target share with 1.89 YPRR, five red zone targets, and a 14.3% first-read share. Henry has three TE1 finishes this season in weekly scoring (TE10, TE7, TE8). Henry is the TE21 in fantasy points per game. Over their last five games, Detroit has allowed the second-most receiving fantasy points per game and the fourth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Henry could be a TE1 this week.

Since Week 4, Tucker Kraft has been the TE7 in fantasy points per game. He has had a 16.1% target share with 1.53 YPRR, eight red zone targets, four deep targets, and an 18.2% first-read share. Kraft will need a score to return TE1-level fantasy production this week. He has a horrible matchup. Over their last five games, Minnesota has allowed the fifth-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 5, Kyle Pitts has been the TE6 in fantasy points per game, but he has turned in stinkers in each of the last two games with a combined 7.9 PPR points. An issue in those games that isn't going away is Michael Penix's poor play. In those games, Pitts had an 18.2% target share and 25% first-read share, but only 50% of his targets were deemed catchable. This explains his 29 receiving yards and 0.63 YPRR. We'll see if Pitts can bounce back this week. Over their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the third-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends. I want to be hopeful, but I just saw Penix crush Pitts against Cincy, who has been unable to stop tight ends all season.

Brenton Strange has been awesome on a per-route basis, but the fact that the Jags have been blowing out teams has limited his production as the TE19 in fantasy points per game. Strange has a 66.3% route share with a 16.2% target share, 2.16 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 17.7% first-read share. Among 41 qualifying tight ends, he is 11th in fantasy points per route run. Strange could be a TE1 this week. Over their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the 13th-most yards per target and the eighth-mos fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Since Week 5, Tyler Higbee has led the tight end room with a 76.8% snap rate, a 65.6% route share, a 10.3% target share, and a 12.8% first-read share. Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen have combined for nine red zone targets during this stretch of games, and Hibee has only one. I could say he's due, but it's also clear the Rams' preference has been to use Parkinson and Allen in the red zone more. Over their last five games, Arizona has faced the fourth-fewest tight end targets, but they are allowing the 13th-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position. Higbee is on the streaming radar this week.

Since Week 7, Chig Okonkwo has been the TE25 in fantasy points per game, with one outing with double-digit PPR points. He has had a 17.2% target share with 1.51 YPRR, one red zone target, and an 18.8% first-read share. Sit Okonkwo this week. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the third-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Overall, Darren Waller is the TE16 in fantasy points per game with two TE1 finishes in weekly scoring (TE5, TE1). Waller has managed four games with double-digit PPR points. Last week, Waller saw a huge spike in his usage with a season-high 67.4% route share, 25.6% target share, and 28.6% first-read share. I don't expect that usage to continue this week, but considering how good Waller was last week, it might be tough for Carolina to put that genie back in the bottle. Overall, Waller has a 54.3% route share, a 9.6% target share, 1.58 YPRR, four red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 10.6% first-read share. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

The Bengals have been a wonderful matchup for tight ends this season, but I'm projecting another down game for Pat Freiermuth this week. The last time he faced Cincy, he secured two of his four targets with 30 scoreless receiving yards. This all goes back to the coverage structure for Cincy. The last time they played Pittsburgh, they utilized single high with 59.5% of their defensive snaps. In three of their last four games, they have utilized single high 52.5-67.4% of their defensive snaps. Freiermuth disappears against single high with a 13% TPRR and 0.98 YPRR. Sit Freiermuth this week.

Last week, Juwan Johnson was the TE10 for the week. Johnson had a 52.8% snap rate and 64.4% route share. That was his highest route share since Week 5. Johnson still only had a 5.7% target share and 9.5% first-read share. His touchdown fueled his fantasy day. Since Week 6, his role in the passing attack has shriveled up with only a 4.9% target share, 0.59 YPRR, and a 7.8% first-read share. Johnson is a sit until his role changes. Over their last five games, Carolina has held tight ends to the 12th-lowest yards per target and the 14th-fewest receiving fantasy points per game.

Mike Gesicki is the TE12 in fantasy points per game, but that is really just fueled by six touchdowns in eight games played. Over the last two games, his role has grown with a 69.4% route share, 10.4% target share, 1.47 YPRR, and a 13.5% first-read share. Gesicki is on the streaming radar again this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the third-most yards per target and the 11th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Dalton Schultz has become a part-time player in the Houston offense. Last week, he had only a 45.5% snap rate and 50% route share. He only managed an 8.1% target share and two receptions. Schultz is a sit until his role changes.

Ok, we're going back to Darnell Washington this week as a streaming option. Yep, you guessed it. It's because of single-high coverage. The last time they played Pittsburgh, they utilized single high with 59.5% of their defensive snaps. In three of their last four games, they have utilized single high 52.5-67.4% of their defensive snaps. The last time Washington faced this defense, he secured three of his four targets with 67 receiving yards (zero touchdowns). Against single high, Washington has a 27% TPRR and 2.72 YPRR. With DK Metcalf dealing with DJ Turner all game, Washington could see a decent workload. Washington is tied for the team lead with seven red zone targets and has three scores this season. He could be a TE1 this week. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the tenth-most yards per target to tight ends while ranking 15th in receiving fantasy points per game.

In Drew Lock's two starts, AJ Barner has finished as the TE20 and TE5 in weekly scoring. With that higher finish, I also have to mention that he scored a rushing touchdown in that game. In those games, Barner had a 9.3% target share, 0.41 YPRR, one red zone target, and a 7.5% first-read share. Barner is a low-end streaming option this week. Over their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the sixth-most receiving fantasy points per game and ranked 19th in fantasy points per opportunity against tight ends.

Mark Andrews is the TE29 in fantasy points per game. Andrews hasn't managed double-digit PPR points since Week 4. Andrews has a 17.4% target share with 1.26 YPRR, seven red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.3% first-read share. Andrews is on the streaming radar this week. Yes, I'm assuming that many people have dropped him at this point in the season. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the most yards per target and the 14th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Brevyn Spann-Ford should take over as Dallas's starting tight end this week with Jake Ferguson sidelined. This season, Spann-Ford has had a 20% TPRR, 1.33 YPRR, two red zone targets, and a 6.1% first-read share in limited duty. Last week, he had a 67.6% route share, a 17.2% target share, 1.24 YPRR (31 receiving yards), and a 23.5% first-read share. He's on the streaming radar this week. The 49ers, over their last five games, have allowed the tenth-most receiving fantasy points per game to tight ends while ranking 18th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed.
